Face aux lacunes persistantes de la couv: Faced with persistent gaps in network coverage across several parts of the national territory, the Minister of Post and Telecommunications, Sid Ali Zerrouki, issued a stern warning to the three Algerian mobile network operators this Wednesday. Sub-standard quality of service will no longer be tolerated below contractual commitments.
Des failles de couverture « inacceptable: "Unacceptable" coverage flaws observed on the groundThe hardening of the government's tone follows several inspection visits by the minister to various wilayas. It was during his visit to Batna on Sunday that Sid Ali Zerrouki personally noted an "unacceptable flaw" in network coverage.
« Sur la route entre la cité Hamla 2 et: "On the road between the Hamla 2 housing estate and the wilaya headquarters, the network is almost non-existent. I personally observed that the call drops," lamented the minister. This situation is all the more problematic as the failures occur near the wilaya headquarters, where coverage should be optimal.
Une autre visite à El Bayadh a confirmé: Another visit to El Bayadh confirmed these alarming findings. The minister gave firm instructions to the operators, emphasizing that "network availability can save lives," especially in the context of an upsurge in road accidents.

Analyse Algeria Tech :Ce durcissement go: Algeria Tech Analysis: This government crackdown marks a turning point in Algerian telecoms policy. After years of warnings without concrete follow-up, the State is finally taking firm action. The minister's findings in Batna and El Bayadh reveal a structural problem: coverage is failing even near wilaya headquarters, raising questions about compliance with contractual commitments over the years.
Le timing est significatif : avec le dép: The timing is significant: with the deployment of 4G across 1,400 rural localities and Algérie Télécom's modernization plans, the government is showing its willingness to catch up on accumulated delays. However, the true measure of success will be the speed at which "dead zones" on vital roadways are corrected. For Algerian citizens, many of whom now depend on mobile for work, education, and essential services, reliable coverage is no longer a luxury but an economic and security necessity.
